transcript.text: This is Swift, an automated flood assistant working with local emergency services. Am I speaking with someone at 524 Glamis Lane?

Yeah, this is me at 524 Glamis Lane, just me and my partner here, no one’s stuck inside or anything, and we’re good to go—no water in the house, and I’ve got a truck to help if needed, just not a boat or any seats
Thanks for confirming your address and safety. How many people are at the home right now, including anyone who can't come to the phone?
There’s two of us here, and neither of us is stuck or can’t come to the phone—just us, no one else, and the water’s not even inside yet.

Thanks for letting us know you’re both safe and reachable. Is there anyone there who can't leave on their own, for example someone who uses a wheelchair, needs oxygen, or is bedbound? If it's a wheelchair, does it have a motor?
No one here can’t leave on their own, and no wheelchairs or medical needs—just us two, fine and able, no trouble at all.
Thanks for letting us know you’re both fine and able. Is there water inside the home right now?
No water inside at all, just us two fine and dry right here at 524 Glamis Lane—no need to rush, we’re good!
If neighbors need a ride out, do you have a high-clearance truck, a boat, or free seats in a vehicle?
Yeah, I’ve got a high-clearance truck that can handle the floodwaters, and I’m happy to give a ride—just let me know if you’re stuck or need to get out, I’ve got you covered.
Thanks for offering help during the flood. Let me read that back: 2 people; no water inside yet; you can help with a truck. Is that right?
Yeah, that’s right—just two of us here, no water in yet, and I’ve got a truck to help with, no problem!

Thanks for confirming your situation is clear right now. I've recorded that you may be able to help neighbors. A dispatcher may contact you. Only go out if it's safe for you, and never drive into water you can't see the bottom of. Goodbye.
